headline: Gen AI Databricks Engineer
text:
N𝗧𝗧 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 asked these 𝗦𝗤𝗟 questions in a Data Engineering interview 
CTC → 𝟮𝟴-𝟯𝟱 𝗟𝗣𝗔 (Difficulty level = Intermediate)

1.⁠ ⁠Write a SQL query to get the daily count of active users (logged in at least once).
2.⁠ ⁠Find the 2nd highest transaction per user without using LIMIT or TOP.
3.⁠ ⁠Identify data gaps in time-series event logs (e.g., missing hourly records).
4.⁠ ⁠Fetch the first purchase date per user and calculate days since then.
5.⁠ ⁠Detect schema changes in SCD Type 2 tables using Delta Lake.
6.⁠ ⁠Join product and transaction tables and filter out null foreign keys safely.
7.⁠ ⁠Get users who upgraded to premium within 7 days of signup.
8.⁠ ⁠Calculate cumulative distinct product purchases per customer.
9.⁠ ⁠Retrieve customers who spent above average in their region.
10.⁠ ⁠Find duplicate rows in an ingestion table (based on all columns).
11.⁠ ⁠Compute daily revenue growth % using lag window function.
12.⁠ ⁠Identify products with declining sales 3 months in a row.
13.⁠ ⁠Get users with at least 3 logins per week over last 2 months.
14.⁠ ⁠Rank users by frequency of login in the current quarter.
15.⁠ ⁠Fetch users who purchased same product multiple times in one day.
16.⁠ ⁠Detect and delete late-arriving data for current month partitions.
17.⁠ ⁠Get top 5 products by profit margin across all categories.
18.⁠ ⁠Compare rolling 30-day revenue vs previous 30-day window.
19.⁠ ⁠Flag transactions happening outside business hours.
20.⁠ ⁠Write an optimized SQL query using broadcast join hints for small lookup tables.

text:
Fine-tuning massive LLMs used to be painfully slow, but not anymore!

4 open source libraries that accelerate fine-tuning of Large Language Models

1. Unsloth AI

• Fine-tune models like Qwen3, Llama 4, and Gemma 3 up to 2× faster with 70% less VRAM
• Uses optimized Triton kernels and manual backprop for exact accuracy
• Supports low-resource setups and runs on consumer GPUs or even Colab/Kaggle with ~3 GB VRAM

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/g4MfgVh3

2. LLaMA Factory

• Fine-tune over 100 models (LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, etc.) using a simple CLI or WebUI
• Supports LoRA, QLoRA, full or frozen fine-tuning across 2–8‑bit precision
• Includes built-in dataset templates, training monitors, and model export options

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/gTpaFzY2

3. DeepSpeed

• Built for large-scale distributed fine-tuning with ZeRO and FSDP
• Optimized for multi-GPU and multi-node training with advanced memory management
• Trusted in production environments for scalable LLM training

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/gUpE66zw

4. Axolotl

• Yaml-based setup for fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, DPO, GRPO, and multimodal workflows
• Includes kernel optimizations for memory-efficient training
• Actively maintained with support for Hugging Face, model export, and inference

GitHub repo → https://lnkd.in/giRYvhsc

Fine-tuning massive LLMs used to be painfully slow, but not anymore.

text:
I’m a Data Scientist & I had to teach myself FastAPI
7 most important things for everyone should know
(also helpful for your interview 👇)

Because deploying AI/ML = building robust APIs.

1️⃣ 𝗜𝘁’𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 “𝗙𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗔𝗣𝗜”
→ It’s actually built on Starlette (handles web requests & async event loops) + Pydantic (validates and parses your data).
✅ That means super fast I/O and strict type checking.
✅ Know async def vs def - your DB calls, external APIs, file reads should be async. 
✅ That’s where you get real performance.

2️⃣ 𝗗𝗼𝗰𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲.
→ FastAPI auto-generates interactive Swagger docs at /docs from your Python type hints.
✅ Your contracts stay always in sync.
✅ Frontend teams, PMs, and even new devs love this - they can test endpoints right in the browser.

3️⃣ 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗶𝗻𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝗿𝗲𝘁 𝘀𝗮𝘂𝗰𝗲.
→ With Depends(get_db), every request gets a fresh DB session.
→ Same pattern for auth checks, reading config, or injecting cache clients.
✅ Keeps your endpoints skinny, testable, and decoupled.

4️⃣ 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝘀𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝘆 𝗣𝘆𝗱𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰.
→ Just define a BaseModel. 
→ FastAPI auto-validates request payloads, auto-serializes your responses, and gives clear error traces.
✅ No more if 'name' not in payload. 
✅ Safer, cleaner, faster APIs.

5️⃣ 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁-𝗶𝗻 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 & 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗵.
→ FastAPI ships with OAuth2, JWT flows, API keys.
✅ Even updates your Swagger UI to show an “Authorize” button.
✅ Know how to use OAuth2PasswordBearer or a Depends(verify_user). 

6️⃣ 𝗠𝗶𝗱𝗱𝗹𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹.
→ Want to log every request? Measure execution time? Enforce CORS across your app? Or even modify headers before they hit your route?
✅ With @app.middleware("http"), you can wrap every single request & response globally.

7️⃣ 𝗟𝗶𝗳𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗻 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 & 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀.
→ Setup resources at startup (like DB connections), clean them on shutdown.
→ Use BackgroundTasks to offload sending emails, logs, or heavy processing after returning a response.
✅ Keeps your app snappy - user doesn’t wait for slow work.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗔𝗜/𝗠𝗟?
Because eventually your model or AI system will live behind an API.
You need to handle inputs, validate them, async call your vector DB, log errors, and return JSON - all reliably.

What did I miss?

I really hope this was useful!
Let's repost to help others 💚

text:
"I thought I knew SQL... until my interviewer asked me these!"
 SQL interviews can be tricky! Here are some thought-provoking questions that tested my knowledge:
 1️⃣ How do you pivot rows into columns in SQL?
 2️⃣ What’s the difference between INNER JOIN and CROSS JOIN?
 3️⃣ How can you delete duplicate rows while keeping only the latest record?
 4️⃣ What are common table expressions (CTEs), and how do they differ from subqueries?
 5️⃣ How do you identify and remove orphan records between two related tables?
 6️⃣ How do you randomly sample 10% of rows from a large table?
 7️⃣ How can you generate running totals without using window functions?
 8️⃣ What’s the difference between RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), and ROW_NUMBER()?
 9️⃣ How do you perform case-insensitive searches in SQL?
 🔟 How do you convert a comma-separated string into individual rows?
 1️⃣1️⃣ How do you find the second highest salary in a department without using TOP or LIMIT?
 1️⃣2️⃣ What’s the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE?
 1️⃣3️⃣ How can you handle NULLs in JOIN conditions effectively?
 1️⃣4️⃣ How would you implement Type 2 Slowly Changing Dimensions using SQL?
 1️⃣5️⃣ How do you traverse a parent-child hierarchy using SQL?
 1️⃣6️⃣ What are the advantages and disadvantages of indexing in SQL?
 1️⃣7️⃣ How can you track changes to sensitive columns like salary or status using SQL only?
 1️⃣8️⃣ What’s the use of CROSS APPLY and OUTER APPLY in SQL Server?
 1️⃣9️⃣ How do you calculate moving averages in SQL?
 2️⃣0️⃣ How do you optimize queries involving multiple OR conditions?
SQL is powerful, but the right questions make you think beyond the basics.
 Which of these do you find the trickiest? Let’s discuss!
